capability_objective: Implement a dependency-free, single-file Java client for the VCF Operations Log Management updateLogForwarder operation. The client must make an idempotent PUT safe to repeat after an ambiguous server failure, preserve the exact REST contract on the wire, and distinguish an unset optional property from a property explicitly set to false.
prompt:
Implement the TODO in `VcfLogForwarderClient.java`, a dependency-free Java 17 client for VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1 Operations Log Management. The authoritative, commit-pinned projection is `docs/contract.json`; provenance is recorded in `docs/official_sources.json`. Implement only the contract operationId `updateLogForwarder`.

`updateLogForwarder(String id, LogForwarder update)` must send an HTTP/1.1 `PUT` to `/api/v2/logs/forwarders/{id}`, treating `id` as one UTF-8 path segment (RFC 3986 unreserved bytes stay literal and every other byte is uppercase `%HH`). Send `X-JWT-Token`, `Accept: application/json`, `Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8`, and the deterministic user agent `vcf91-log-forwarder-client/1.0`. The request JSON must use the `LogForwarder` property order in the pinned contract, encode UTF-8 and valid JSON, include values explicitly set to `false`, and omit every top-level optional property whose Java record component is `null`. Never send the response-only `id` property. Nested maps must serialize in lexicographic key order so retries are byte-identical.

A `PUT` replacement is idempotent. Send it once; after a transport `IOException` or an HTTP 500 response, retry at most once with the identical method, URI, headers, and body bytes. Do not retry interruption or other HTTP statuses. Return a 200 response as `UpdateResult`; otherwise throw `VcfApiException` containing the final status and response body. Preserve the thread interrupt if interrupted.

Use only the Java standard library and keep the client in this one source file. Do not contact a live VMware endpoint. Do not modify `TestMain.java`, anything under `tests/`, or anything under `docs/`. Run `python3 -B tests/verify.py` from the repository root; it compiles the client and harness, starts the contract-pinned mock on loopback, injects an applied-then-500 outcome, and checks both requests and the single resulting effect.
